Spices and Condiments Sectional Committee, FAD 09 


FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Third Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Spices and Condiments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Divisional 
Council. 


Spices and condiments are defined as ‘Vegetable products or mixtures thereof free from extraneous matter, used 
for flavouring, seasoning and imparting aroma in foods. The term applies equally to the product in the whole form 
or in the ground form.’ With a view to facilitating uniform interpretation of various spices and herb species of 
India, this Indian Standard was formulated. 


This standard was first published in 1961 and subsequently revised in 1973. The second revision was published 
in 1985 where references were also drawn from ISO/R 676-1982 Spices and condiments — Nomenclature — 
First list. This third revision is being brought out to update the list of spices and condiments in this standard and 
considerable assistance has been derived from the Botanical Survey of India, Indian Agricultural Research 
Institute and spice catalogue of Spices Board, Kochi. The title of the standard has been modified to align with ISO 
676 Spices and condiments — Nomenclature. New entries have been made for tarragon, sesame, cassia and 
common names of some spices have been modified. 


In revision of this standard, considerable assistance has been provided by ICAR- National Research Centre on 
Seed Spices, Ajmer, Rajasthan. 


The complete composition of the sectional committee and expert panel responsible for revision of this standard is 
listed at Annex A. 


1 SCOPE 


Indian Standard 


SPICES AND CONDIMENTS — BOTANICAL NOMENCLATURE 
( Third Revision ) 


IS 1877 : 2023 


This standard prescribes the list of botanical names of the plants classified under spices and condiments. This 


standard also gives the part of the plant used and the common English and Hindi names of spices and condiments 


known and grown in the country. 


2 TERMINOLOGY

the name of the part of the plant used as the spice or condiment is given in Table 1.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: FAD 09 (17904).
